assets.name: Emerging Markets

assets.name: Silver
why: Year 1 (2027): Goldman Sachs projects $85–$100 range for 2026 average (latest June 2026 reports); J.P. Morgan sees $81 average for 2026. Using $85 as year-end 2026/early 2027 target per multiple bank consensus.

Year 2 (2028): UBS expects silver to decline toward $85/oz around March 2027, then consolidates. HSBC forecasts $75 average for 2026, $68 for 2027 (June 2026 data). Conservative estimates suggest $75 for 2028 reflecting supply deficit persistence but cyclical consolidation.

Year 3 (2029): Silver supercycle thesis projects $70–$120 for 2028 per MintBuilder research; structural solar demand (200+ million oz/year) supports mid-range of $90 for 2028 reflecting tightening supply-demand balance as depletion accelerates.

assets.name: Palladium
why: Year 1 (2027): TD Securities projects 2026 palladium at $1,819/oz average (January 26, 2026). WalletInvestor projects $1,604 for end-2026 with sustained uptrend to ~$2,368 by year-end 2027 driven by catalytic converter demand and supply tightness.

Year 2 (2028): J2T analysis shows 2027 range $2,356–$3,290; World Platinum Investment Council projects deficits through 2027. Taking $2,368 as 2027 target per WalletInvestor, extrapolating modest 5% growth to ~$2,486 for 2028 as EV adoption accelerates but recycling grows.

Year 3 (2029): CoinPriceForecast maintains bullish trajectory reaching $3,290 in 2027; LongForecast projects bearish $2,356. Mid-case scenario: $2,500 for 2028 reflecting 2027–2028 transition from structural deficit (pre-2024 pattern) to potential 2029+ surplus as EV penetration reaches 22–25%.

assets.name: WTI Crude Oil
why: Year 1 (2027): Goldman Sachs forecasts Brent/WTI to average $56/$52 for 2026 (December 2025 outlook), recovering to $80/$76/bbl by late 2028. Implies 2026 bottom mid-year then recovery; using $75 for end-2026/2027 transition per Goldman's base case recovery trajectory.

Year 2 (2028): Goldman Sachs explicitly forecasts WTI to reach $76/bbl by late 2028 (December 2025 Outlook). Taking $76 for 2028 reflecting gradual rebalancing as supply deficits emerge in 2027H2 per Goldman's assumption.

Year 3 (2029): Extrapolating from Goldman's late-2028 $76 target with modest 2.6% annual growth reflecting structural energy demand (1.2mb/d growth in 2026 per Goldman), yields ~$78. Conservative mid-range estimate of $76 for 2028 holds through 2029 as market balances.
